key_insight: HamGNN-NEGF uses a machine-learned DFT Hamiltonian plus efficient Green’s-function solvers to deliver near-DFT transport accuracy with linear scaling in device length.
engineering_relevance: This makes predictive quantum transport feasible for realistic nanoelectronic devices with thousands to over 10,000 atoms at dramatically lower cost than self-consistent DFT-NEGF.
method: Train an E(3)-equivariant GNN on conventional DFT Hamiltonians for small structures.
Predict large-device Hamiltonians and combine them with DFT-derived electrode self-energies.
Use nonorthogonal kernel polynomial methods and recursive Green’s functions to compute transport efficiently.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports meV-level Hamiltonian accuracy, faithful transmission spectra, and speedups exceeding three orders of magnitude on Pt-Si-Pt, doped Pt-Si:P-Pt, and Pt-molecule-Pt benchmarks, including systems beyond 10,000 atoms.
watch_item: The zero-bias Hamiltonian approximation for finite-bias transport is stated to be reliable only in weakly nonlinear regimes.
paper_title: Linear-Scaling Quantum Transport from Machine-Learning Density Functional Theory Hamiltonians
